---
name: sgt-plan
description: Use when you (an AI coding agent) are about to implement a multi-step task in an sgt-tracked repo and want your intent recorded as a plan that the sgt graph can check your work against. Teaches the draft -> work -> checkpoint -> done loop over the MCP tools (sgt_plan_intake, sgt_checkpoint, sgt_drift, sgt_plan_done), and how to own a session when several agents work concurrently. This is the on-ramp: the agent drafts the plan, not the human.
---

# Drafting and closing an sgt plan

In sgt, a *plan* is your stated intent recorded before you do the work: a list of predicted
steps, each an off-chain "hollow" op that never touches the real op DAG. As you edit code, sgt
mines real ops and matches them back to your predicted steps. This is how the graph shows whether
what you built matches what you intended, and what happened outside any plan.

You draft the plan. The human does not write it. Your job is to record intent up front, then let
sgt reconcile it against the code you actually produce. The materialized code is always the source
of truth: a mismatch between plan and code is information, never an error to "fix" by rewriting the
plan.

## The loop

1. **Draft** — call `sgt_plan_intake` with your plan text and an explicit `session_id` you own
   (see ownership below). Decompose the task into concrete steps, one per unit of work, each named
   at the granularity you'll build it (a `file::Symbol`, or a bare `file` when a step spans a whole
   module). Intake mines the working tree first, so its baseline reflects current reality.

2. **Work** — implement the steps in the working tree (or a `sgt session` worktree). Edit code
   normally; you do not touch the plan while working.

3. **Checkpoint** — call `sgt_checkpoint` (no args) for a read-only preview of which mined ops
   overlap which pending steps, plus any drift. When a group is right, call `sgt_checkpoint` again
   with `confirm: [{hollow_ids, op_ids}]` to record it. The step flips to `matched`. Nothing is
   confirmed unless you name the group, so preview freely.

4. **Done** — a session closes itself the moment its last step is confirmed. Call `sgt_plan_done`
   with your `session_id` only for the leftover case: steps you ended up building differently than
   predicted, which will never match. `plan_done` closes the session so it stops showing as active;
   the record stays as completed history. (To discard a plan entirely, that is `sgt plan abandon`
   on the CLI, not `plan_done`.)

Between steps 3 and 4, `sgt_drift` lists ops no active plan predicted. Drift is not a chore to
resolve; it is a read-only diff of what happened outside your stated plan. Read it to confirm no
unplanned change crept in, then land the work as usual.

## Session ownership when agents work concurrently

Several agents can have live plans at once. Each session is owned by exactly one agent:

- **Pick a distinct `session_id`** at intake that identifies your task (a stable slug, e.g. your
  agent/task name). Never reuse another agent's id.
- **Only confirm or close your own session.** `sgt_checkpoint`'s matching is scoped per session
  (each session only matches ops mined since its own baseline against its own steps), so confirming
  a group in your session never disturbs another agent's. Do not call `sgt_plan_done` on a session
  you did not open.
- Concurrent sessions all appear in the graph as separate active plans. Finishing them one by one
  is the expected shape: each agent drafts, builds, checkpoints, and closes its own.

## Writing good steps

- One step per coherent unit of work; name the entity or file it will touch.
- Prefer `file::Symbol` granularity when you know the symbol (`crdt.py::RGA`), a bare `file`
  (`server.py`) when the step is whole-module. The matcher joins on the qualname (file is treated
  as a guess that may drift) or on file scope for a bare-file step.
- Do not predict test names or incidental helpers you can't foresee; those surface as drift, which
  is fine.

## Redesign A–E — plan lifecycle + calmer, honest UI (2026-07-24)

The screenshots that opened this exposed one root problem wearing several costumes: **finished plans
never left the "active" surface, so the sidebar, status bar, and CodeLens all read as a pile of unresolved
chores.** The `blame JOURNAL.md failed` spam was a second, unrelated symptom (blame on an unmapped file).
Fixed as five workstreams. None of this touches livehub content — it's the sgt repo + extension, and all
of it stays **uncommitted** per mandate.

**A — plan lifecycle (backend root cause).** A plan session had no terminal state: every step matched but
the session stayed `active` forever, so `active_sessions()` returned everything ever intake'd. Fixes in
`sgt/loop/plan.py` + `match.py` + `sgt/cli/loop.py` + `sgt/mcp/server.py`:
  - `confirm_match` now sets a session `completed` once it has no pending steps.
  - `active_sessions()` filters to `status == active` (finished plans stop cluttering every view).
  - dead `sweep_stale_sessions` wired into `intake` (abandons sessions idle past the TTL).
  - new `sgt plan done <session>` CLI verb + `sgt_plan_done` MCP tool to close a session explicitly.
  This is *the* fix — the UI clutter was downstream of a missing state transition, not a rendering problem.
  Tests updated to the new contract (single-step sessions complete on confirm and leave the active surface;
  matched-span provenance now asserted against `_load_sessions`, and a two-step session preserves the
  still-active matched-span case). `test_server.py` / `test_cli.py` / `test_api.py` green.

**B — drift is a read-only diff, not a chore.** `changesTree.ts` rewritten from a "Trust queue /
Acknowledge" action list into two read-only sections: *Unplanned changes* (drift) and *Untracked files*.
Removed the `trust` section, `trustGroup`/`trustOp` node kinds, and the `Acknowledge` affordance. CodeLens
+ diff copy reframed ("◇ unplanned change (not in the active plan)"). The principle: **actual code >
planned** — drift is just what the tree shows that no plan predicted; you read it, you don't resolve it.

**C — agents draft plans, humans don't.** New `.claude/skills/sgt-plan/SKILL.md` teaches an agent the
intake → work → checkpoint → `plan done` loop over MCP, with a session-ownership convention so concurrent
agents each own a distinct `session_id` and only close their own. Answers the "should a human write plans?"
question: no — the agent drafts in sgt format, the graph shows it, agents finish steps one by one.

**D — minimal UI pass.** Feature rail now expands subsystems by default (a collapsed rail read as empty);
status bar quieted to one `$(checklist) Plan m/t` aggregate (dropped the ○●○● glyph run and the always-on
`◆drift` badge — drift moved to the tooltip); em-dashes purged from persistent chrome (status bar,
package.json, workbench drift chip). Deliberately did **not** collapse the per-session plan chips into one
strip: with A's active-only filter the remaining chips are real concurrent agents, which the user
explicitly wants to see. `workbench.css` audited and left untouched — already dial-compliant (theme tokens,
one accent, reduced-motion block).

**E — simpler command surface.** Rare proposal verbs (`proposeLand`/`proposePublish`/`viewProposal`)
rehomed to a `semi-git (advanced)` palette category; the daily spine stays top-level. The
`sgt.reviewAck` command was **removed outright** rather than demoted: B deleted its only entry point (the
trust-queue context menu), and from the palette it was a silent no-op (it needs a node's op-ids). Cleaned up
the orphans it left — the handler in `commands.ts`, the `reviewAck` seam + `ReviewAckResult` import in

# Consequence Focus Pane — interactive preview→confirm for sgt mutating verbs

## Context

Running an sgt mutating verb today either applies blind (`--json`/non-tty) or prints a
wall of feedforward text and asks `[y/N]` (`sgt/cli/ideal_edit.py::_emit_verb_result`).
The text lists *what is touched* ("also affects feature G, E") — data, not consequence.
A programmer at a decision point wants the **consequence**: what breaks, what they must
do next, and whether they can back out. The blast list without that framing reads as
"…so what?".

**Goal:** when a user runs a mutating verb on a terminal, the confirm step *is* a focused,
minimal, visual pane rendered like a zoomed region of `sgt log` — ENTER = apply,
SPACE = toggle a fallout item (adjust), ESC = abort — leading with a one-line "so-what"
sentence. **Hard constraint from the user: no new CLI flags or subcommands.** The pane
replaces the existing `[y/N]` prompt for a plain tty invocation; `--json` / `--emit` /
`--yes` / non-tty keep their current meaning (machine + immediate-apply contract that
VS Code and tests depend on — must stay byte-for-byte).

**Design principle:** partition affected items by "must the user act?". Promote
`blast` / `fork` / oracle-fail to the pane; **hide the mechanical `carry` bucket** (a quiet
count only); show `foundation` only when it blocks. One color (the anchor lane), three
states (stays / removed-or-hole / anchor).

## Scope of this implementation

The **so-what layer** and the **interactive pane** are built once and are verb-agnostic.
This PR wires only the **ideal-edit family** — the verbs routed through `_emit_verb_result`,
which already have a pure, side-effect-free `plan_*` preview:

- `revert`, `restore`
- `revert --session <name>`, `revert <lane> --to <commit>`, `revert <feature>@<n>` / `:slug`

These deliver the "run command → see pane" experience with no new args and no core changes.

**Deferred (out of scope here), because each needs new preview machinery:**
- `feature merge/split/rename/move` — reversible, metadata-only; have `plan_*` previews but a
  different (non-`_project_verb_preview`) shape that must be projected into the shared shape first.
- `sync` / `land` / `propose` / `resolve` — these apply immediately then project the *result*;
  gating them needs a **core dry-run** (e.g. `plan_sync` that computes would-be forks without
  writing `.sgt/forks.json`; a land oracle-verdict pass that does not advance the branch record).
  Noted for a later phase; not built now.

## Approach

### 1. Pure "so-what" layer in `sgt/api.py`

Add pure functions over the existing projection dict, near `_frontier_rows` (~457), so every
surface (CLI, TUI, VS Code) that reads `_project_verb_preview` / `verb_preview_view` inherits
them for free:

- `_reversible(verb) -> bool` — table-driven; revert/restore/after/merge/split/rename/move = True,
  default False.
- `_carry_count(projected) -> int` — count `frontier` rows with `bucket == "carry"` (the hidden
  mechanical repoints).
- `_fallout_rows(projected) -> list[dict]` — **act-required only**: toggleable `blast` frontier ops
  + one `fork` row per forked symbol. Excludes `carry` and `foundation`.
- `so_what_for(projected, kept=frozenset()) -> str` — the one-line consequence, recomputed live as
  the kept-set changes. Pure (only the dict + caller's kept op-ids). Templates:

  | verb | condition | sentence |
  |---|---|---|
  | revert | ok, no blast | `Removes {primary}. Nothing depends on it — clean revert. Undo-able.` |
  | revert | ok, N blast, K kept | `{primary} will break — {N-K} dependent(s) to re-draft[, keeping {K}]. Undo-able.` |
  | revert | refused/forked | `Won't apply — revert of {primary} would fork it. Resolve the fork first (sgt resolve {primary}).` |
  | restore | ok, no blast | `Re-adds {primary} and its prerequisites. Nothing to reconcile. Undo-able.` |
  | restore | ok, N blast | `Re-adds {primary}; {N} dependent(s) return with it. Undo-able.` |

  `primary` = `affected_symbols[0]` if present else `target`. Carry is never named.

Then in `_project_verb_preview` (~525), before `return`, merge four keys onto the dict:
`reversible`, `carry_count`, `fallout`, `so_what` (with `kept=∅` default).

### 2. CLI→TUI bridge — new module `sgt/tui/consequence.py`

Isolates the optional `textual` import behind a lazy import (same boundary `sgt/tui/app.py::run`
already uses). Exports:

- `Decision` — frozen dataclass `{apply: bool, kept: frozenset[str]}`.
- `ConsequenceApp(App[Decision])` — a small **value-returning** app (NOT the heavy `SgtTui`
  browser, which boots mining/clustering in `on_mount` and returns `None`). Textual's idiom is
  `App[T].run() -> return_value` set via `App.exit(value)`. Composition:
  - **so_what Static** (top, bold) — recomputed on each toggle via `sgt.api.so_what_for(pview, self._kept)`.
  - **rail Static** — `render_verb_preview_lines(...)` output (the existing checkpoint-rail +
    also-affected feedforward), same `Text.from_ansi` pattern as `GraphScreen._body()`.
  - **fallout DataTable** (only if toggleable `blast` rows exist) — marker (`✓`/` `) + short op-id +
    `will break`/`kept`. `space` toggles the op-id into `self._kept`. Marker/fill/toggle mirror
    `FrontierScreen._fill`/`action_toggle` (~20 lines duplicated, not abstracted — no second caller,
    per CLAUDE.md §3); counts via existing `sgt.tui.app.frontier_counts`.
  - **footer Label** — `enter apply · space keep · esc leave` (+ quiet `{carry_count} auto-repoint`
    when >0).
  - Bindings: `enter`→`action_apply` (`priority=True` so DataTable doesn't swallow it) →
    `self.exit(Decision(True, frozenset(self._kept)))`; `space`→toggle; `escape`→
    `self.exit(Decision(False))`.
- `run_consequence(pview, map_view, grid_view, segments, *, focus_fid) -> Decision` — blocking
  one-shot; CLI passes already-fetched views (no recompute).

### 3. Gate in `sgt/cli/ideal_edit.py::_emit_verb_result` (~124)

Replace **only** the interactive `input()` portion of the existing plain-text-apply branch. No new
argparse args. The `--json` immediate-apply tail and the non-tty exit-2 refusal stay unchanged:

- Build `pview = _project_verb_preview(repo, preview)` and fetch `map_view/grid_view/segments_view`
  (already imported in this branch).
- If `not yes and stdin.isatty() and stdout.isatty()`: lazily
  `from sgt.tui.consequence import run_consequence`; on `ImportError` (textual absent) fall through
  to the current `render_verb_preview_lines` + `input()` degrade path.
- On a `Decision`: `apply=False` → print "skipped", return 1; `apply=True` → `_apply_decision(...)`.
- `_apply_decision(repo, preview, kept, focus_fid)` bridges the kept-set onto **existing** machinery:
  a non-empty `kept` on a `revert` routes to `_revert_keep_dependents(..., keep=frozenset(kept))`
  (the current `--keep` continuation-hollow path); otherwise `verbs.apply(repo, preview)`. This
  covers every verb in the family through one gate.

## Critical files

- `sgt/api.py` — add `_reversible`, `_carry_count`, `_fallout_rows`, `so_what_for`; merge 4 keys
  into `_project_verb_preview`.
- `sgt/tui/consequence.py` — **new**: `Decision`, `ConsequenceApp(App[Decision])`, `run_consequence`.
- `sgt/cli/ideal_edit.py` — gate + `_apply_decision` inside `_emit_verb_result` (no new args).
- `sgt/tui/graph.py` — reused as-is (`render_verb_preview_lines` for the rail).
- `sgt/tui/app.py` — reused as-is (`frontier_counts`; `FrontierScreen` as the toggle pattern).

## Verification

- **Pure layer** — `tests/test_so_what.py` (new): `so_what_for` over hand-built dicts for every
  template row (clean/N-blast/kept-adjusted/forked revert, restore); assert exact sentences and that
  `kept` flips "will break" → "keeping K". Extend an api test to build a seeded corpus (as
  `tests/tui/test_app_interactions.py::_seed` does), run `verb_preview_view(repo, "revert", <sym>)`,
  assert `fallout` has the blast op-ids, **excludes** carry, `carry_count` matches, `reversible` True.
- **Textual screen** — `tests/tui/test_consequence.py` (new, `pytest.importorskip("textual")`): drive
  `ConsequenceApp` with `async with app.run_test() as pilot`; `space` on a blast row updates
  `app._kept` and the so_what text; `enter` → `return_value == Decision(True, {...})`; fresh app +
  `escape` → `Decision(False)`.
- **CLI gate contract** — extend the ideal-edit CLI tests: monkeypatch `run_consequence` to return
  apply/abort and assert `verbs.apply` fires / exit 1; monkeypatch `isatty`→False and assert the
  render+exit-2 degrade path and `--json` immediate-apply are byte-unchanged.
- **Manual** — in a tty: `sgt revert <feature>` shows the pane; toggle a dependent with space (so-what
  updates), enter applies with `--keep` semantics; `sgt revert <x> --json` still applies immediately.
- Run focused per-file (per memory `test-suite-slow-subprocess`): `pytest tests/test_so_what.py
  tests/tui/test_consequence.py -q`.

def _chain_repo(tmp_path):
    """helper <- user <- caller: reverting `user` makes `caller` a toggleable blast dependent,
    so the pane shows a fallout row to toggle."""
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    gb, _ = init_store(repo)
    (repo / "a.py").write_text("def helper():\n    return 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    gb.commit_all("helper")
    (repo / "b.py").write_text("from a import helper\n\ndef user():\n    return helper()\n", encoding="utf-8")
    gb.commit_all("user")
    (repo / "c.py").write_text("from b import user\n\ndef caller():\n    return user()\n", encoding="utf-8")
    gb.commit_all("caller")
    get(repo)
    build_map(repo)
    return repo

def _project_feature_preview(repo, verb: str, preview) -> dict:
    """Project a metadata-only feature-reorg preview (`merge`/`rename`/`move`/`split`) into the
    shared consequence shape the pane and `so_what_for` consume. These verbs touch no code, so
    `fallout` and `carry_count` are empty and `reversible` is always True; the projection instead
    carries a short human `summary` (resolved labels, counts, the split groups) the pane renders in
    place of the code rail. Only call on an `ok` preview -- a refusal is handled by the CLI's
    `_fail_preview` before this point."""
    from sgt.lens.tree import load as load_tree

    nodes = (load_tree(repo) or {}).get("nodes", {})

    def label(fid: str) -> str:
        return (nodes.get(fid) or {}).get("label") or fid[:8]

    if verb == "merge":
        primary = label(preview.survivor_id)
        summary = [f"absorb {label(preview.absorbed_id)} → {primary}",
                   f"{preview.op_count} op(s) · {preview.member_count} member(s)"]
    elif verb == "rename":
        primary = preview.new_label
        summary = [f"{preview.old_label!r} → {preview.new_label!r}"]
    elif verb == "move":
        primary = label(preview.target_id)
        summary = [f"{len(preview.op_ids)} op(s) → {primary}"]
    elif verb == "split":
        primary = label(preview.feature_id)
        g0, g1 = preview.groups or ((), ())
        summary = [
            f"{primary} splits in two:",
            f"  keep ({len(g0)}): {', '.join(sorted(g0)[:6])}" + (" …" if len(g0) > 6 else ""),
            f"  new  ({len(g1)}): {', '.join(sorted(g1)[:6])}" + (" …" if len(g1) > 6 else ""),
            f"→ mints {preview.new_id[:8]}",
        ]
    else:  # pragma: no cover -- only the four reorg verbs are projected here
        primary, summary = verb, []

    projected = {
        "ok": True, "verb": verb, "target": primary,
        "affected_symbols": [primary] if primary else [],
        "forked": False, "message": getattr(preview, "message", ""),
        "files": {}, "fallout": [], "carry_count": 0, "reversible": True,
        "summary": summary,
    }
    projected["so_what"] = so_what_for(projected)
    return projected

def render_collab_preview_lines(preview_view: dict, *, color: bool = True) -> list[str]:
    """The **feedforward** graph for a shared-state advance -- `land` (and, later, `sync`/`propose
    land`) -- drawn before the one-way step runs. Unlike a revert's checkpoint rail, the consequence
    here is *where your work is going and what stops it*: the op count it would advance the branch
    by, any same-symbol fork that BLOCKS the advance (with the exact `sgt merge-op` remedy), and the
    LAW-G oracle gate the confirm will run. Pure over the `_project_land_preview` dict; the `[y/N]`
    prompt stays in the CLI caller. A refused/unclean plan (`clean` False) renders its `error`
    alone."""
    verb = preview_view.get("verb", "land")
    branch = preview_view.get("target", "")
    forks = preview_view.get("forks", []) or []
    contradictions = preview_view.get("pin_contradictions", []) or []
    cycles = preview_view.get("declared_cycles", []) or []
    advisory = preview_view.get("advisory")

    if not preview_view.get("clean", True):
        return [f" {_paint('#cc5500', '✗', color=color)} {_bold('land', color=color)}  "
                f"{_dim(branch, color=color)}",
                "",
                _dim(f"   {preview_view.get('error', 'not landable')}", color=color)]

    ops_added = preview_view.get("ops_added", 0)
    lines: list[str] = [
        f" {_paint('#5fafff', '▸', color=color)} {_bold(verb, color=color)}  "
        f"{_bold(branch, color=color)}  {_dim('advance the shared branch', color=color)}",
        "",
        f"   {_paint('#5fafff', '↑', color=color)} your work adds "
        f"{_bold(str(ops_added), color=color)} op(s) to {branch}",
        "",
    ]

    if forks:
        lines.append(_paint("#ffaf00", f"   ⚠ {len(forks)} fork(s) block the land -- "
                                       f"reconcile before it can advance:", color=color))
        for sym, a, b in forks[:8]:
            remedy = _dim(f"sgt merge-op {a[:8]} {b[:8]}", color=color)
            lines.append(f"       {_paint('#ffaf00', sym, color=color)}   {remedy}")
        if len(forks) > 8:
            lines.append(_dim(f"       +{len(forks) - 8} more fork(s)", color=color))
        lines.append("")

    for c in contradictions:
        lines.append(_paint("#ffaf00", f"   ⚠ pin contradiction: {c.get('detail', '')}", color=color))
    for pair in cycles:
        lines.append(_paint("#ffaf00", f"   ⚠ declared-edge cycle: {pair}", color=color))
    if contradictions or cycles:
        lines.append("")

    # The LAW-G gate: name what the confirm will (or won't) do. A fork short-circuits before the
    # oracle; no oracle configured refuses outright; otherwise the oracle runs the tests on confirm.
    if not preview_view.get("oracle_configured", True):
        lines.append(_paint("#ff5f5f", "   oracle: none configured -- land refuses to advance an "
                                       "unverified op-set (LAW-G)", color=color))
    elif forks:
        lines.append(_dim("   oracle: not reached -- the fork blocks the land first", color=color))
    else:
        lines.append(_dim("   oracle: green required -- runs the tests on confirm, then CAS onto "
                          "the tip", color=color))

    if advisory:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(_paint("#ffaf00", f"   ⚠ {advisory}", color=color))

    lines.append("")
    if forks:
        tail = f" won't advance -- {len(forks)} fork(s) to resolve first"
    elif not preview_view.get("oracle_configured", True):
        tail = " won't advance -- no oracle to verify against (LAW-G)"
    else:
        tail = f" advances {branch} by {ops_added} op · runs tests on confirm · not auto-undoable"
    lines.append(_dim(f" {tail.strip()}", color=color))
    return lines

    """Show the land feedforward on a tty and return the user's choice (True apply / False abort).
    The dry-run (`land_preview_view`: `ingest -> resolve`, no oracle, no CAS, rolled back to leave no
    trace) drives the same consequence pane the ideal-edit verbs use -- so the pane renders the
    collaboration graph (`summary`) and the "so what?" line, with no toggleable fallout (a fork is a

    is absent. Called only on an interactive tty."""
    import sys

    from sgt.api import land_preview_view

    from ._common import maybe_confirm

    pview = land_preview_view(repo, branch)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SyncPlan:
    """The dry-run consequence of a `sync` (plan U19/D4): what folding in the teammate's branch
    *would* bring -- computed with `fetch -> ingest -> resolve` (no `materialize`, so the working
    tree and local branch never move), then rolled back to leave no trace (R7). Unlike `land`, a
    fork does not block a sync -- the fork-free part still merges and the fork surfaces as state --
    so `forks` here is *what would surface*, not a blocker. `up_to_date` short-circuits when the
    fetch finds nothing new."""

    remote: str
    branch: str
    up_to_date: bool = False
    ops_added: int = 0
    forks: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()
    pin_contradictions: tuple[Contradiction, ...] = ()
    declared_cycles: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
    base_recovery: str = "none"
    theirs_recovery: str = "mined"


def plan_sync(repo: str | Path, remote: str | None = None, branch: str | None = None) -> SyncPlan:
    """Dry-run a `sync` (D4): fetch the teammate's branch and run `ingest -> resolve` to compute what
    the merge *would* bring in -- incoming op count, any same-symbol fork that would surface, pin/
    declared-edge issues, and the recovery modes -- then roll the transactional local caches back so
    the preview leaves no trace (R7). Skips `materialize` entirely (the only stage that moves the
    working tree or the local branch), so a feedforward pane can show the consequence before the
    merge lands. Mirrors `sync`'s own `ops_added` so the preview predicts the report."""
    repo = Path(repo)
    gb = GitBinding(repo)

    fetched = _fetch.fetch(repo, gb, remote, branch)
    if fetched.up_to_date:
        return SyncPlan(remote=fetched.remote, branch=fetched.branch, up_to_date=True)

    local_before = _snapshot_local_caches(repo)
    try:
        ing = _ingest.ingest(repo, gb, fetched.theirs_sha, fetched.ours_sha, branch=fetched.branch)
        res = _resolve.resolve(repo, ing)
        return SyncPlan(
            remote=fetched.remote, branch=fetched.branch, ops_added=ing.ops_added,
            forks=res.forks, pin_contradictions=res.pin_contradictions,
            declared_cycles=res.declared_cycles,
            base_recovery=ing.base_recovery, theirs_recovery=ing.theirs_recovery,
        )
    finally:
        _restore_local_caches(repo, local_before)

# -- plan_sync: the side-effect-free dry run behind the `sgt sync` feedforward pane ------------

def _committed_state(repo: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    """A byte snapshot of everything a sync would materialize: `main.py` plus every committed `.sgt`
    file, excluding the append-only op store (`.sgt/ops/`) and the derived local caches
    (`.sgt/local/`) that `plan_sync` rolls back on its own. A dry run must leave this byte-identical."""
    state_map: dict[str, bytes] = {}
    main = repo / "main.py"
    if main.is_file():
        state_map["main.py"] = main.read_bytes()
    for p in sorted((repo / ".sgt").rglob("*")):
        if not p.is_file():
            continue
        rel = p.relative_to(repo).as_posix()
        if rel.startswith(".sgt/ops/") or rel.startswith(".sgt/local/") or p.name.startswith(".tmp-"):
            continue
        state_map[rel] = p.read_bytes()
    return state_map


def test_plan_sync_predicts_the_fold_and_leaves_no_trace(tmp_path):
    """The dry run (`fetch -> ingest -> resolve`, no `materialize`) reports the op count a sync would
    fold in, and -- like a blocked land (R7) -- rolls back so the working tree, the committed `.sgt`
    state, and the local branch tip stay byte-identical. A following real sync folds in exactly the
    predicted op count."""
    a, b = _two_clones(tmp_path, _BASE)
    _edit_and_commit(a, "main.py", "def foo():\n    return 100\n\n\ndef bar():\n    return 2\n", "bump foo")
    _push(a)

    gb = GitBinding(b)
    before_head = gb.head()
    lens.get(b)  # settle mine-on-contact caches first, so the snapshot below is the steady state
    before_state = _committed_state(b)

    plan = sync.plan_sync(b, remote="origin", branch="main")

    assert plan.ops_added > 0 and not plan.forks
    assert gb.head() == before_head  # the local branch did not move
    assert _committed_state(b) == before_state  # no trace (R7)

    report = sync.sync(b, remote="origin", branch="main")
    assert report.merged and report.ops_added == plan.ops_added  # the dry run predicted the real fold

sgt advanced forks                  # open forks, and the merge-op that resolves each one
sgt push [remote] [branch]          # push, and tell you to run sgt sync if it gets rejected
sgt land <branch>                   # advance a shared branch to a verified op set

its `--tree`/(default grid)/`--rail`/`--summary` modes. The daily spine stays top-level; rare and
maintenance verbs live under `sgt advanced` and `sgt feature`. `sgt feature regroup merge/split/move`
and `sgt feature rename` only change labels in the feature tree. `sgt advanced merge-op`, `split-op`,
and `transplant` change the actual chain of ops. The names look similar but the jobs are different.

    """Monotonic ``F<n>`` ids that never collide with an existing feature id -- start past the
    largest ``F<n>`` already in `old_ids` so a birth never reuses a dead feature's id. Retained for

    minted two different new ids for one old id, the union holds both `(old, new1)` and
    `(old, new2)` -- a genuine collision. Pick a deterministic winner (smallest content hash) and
    add explicit `loser -> winner` edges, so *every* reference (the old id, or either minted new id)
    resolves to the single canonical feature. Commutative, idempotent, and identical on every
    replica -- no wall clock, no sync-order dependence."""
    merged = set(ours) | set(theirs)

    for old, new in merged:

        *closed* a symbol is found by walking the path's own history -- a pure function of git

    def blob_bytes_many(self, specs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[bytes | None]:
        """Raw bytes for many ``(sha, path)`` pairs, aligned with ``specs`` order -- the batched
        counterpart to ``blob_bytes``. Mining one commit needs many blobs at once (every tracked
        file for ``tree_at``, or every changed file for a diff); one subprocess per blob made
        mining scale as O(commits x files) subprocess spawns. All reads go through the repo's
        one persistent ``git cat-file --batch`` process (``<rev>:<path>`` object specs, so no
        oid lookup is needed first) -- even the per-batch spawn this method used to pay was the
        dominant mining cost at hundreds of batches per history chunk.

        A spec whose rev or path contains a newline can't be framed as a ``<rev>:<path>`` line in
        that pipe protocol -- it would split into two requests and silently desync the shared
        stream for every later reader in the process -- so it detours through a one-shot ``git
        show`` argv read. Newlines in tracked paths are legal in git trees and exotic in practice,
        but the tool's bar is that a read never errors on a noisy repo."""
        if not specs:
            return []
        results: list[bytes | None] = [None] * len(specs)
        batchable: list[tuple[int, tuple[str, str]]] = []
        for i, (rev, path) in enumerate(specs):
            if "\n" in rev or "\n" in path:
                results[i] = self._show_blob(rev, path)  # argv: immune to newline framing
            else:
                batchable.append((i, (rev, path)))
        if batchable:
            batched = _batch_for(self.repo).read_many([spec for _, spec in batchable])
            for (i, _), value in zip(batchable, batched):
                results[i] = value
        return results

    def _show_blob(self, sha: str, path: str) -> bytes | None:
        """One-shot raw-bytes read of ``path`` at ``sha`` via ``git show`` argv -- the fallback
        `blob_bytes_many` uses for a spec a newline makes unframeable in the shared batch pipe.
        Never text-decodes, so a binary blob comes back as its bytes rather than raising."""
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(self.repo), "show", f"{sha}:{path}"], capture_output=True

# memoized read, leaving the dir mtime unchanged, and recounting dirents (cheap, one readdir)
# catches any add/remove that slipped through that tick. (A count-neutral in-place rewrite within
# the same tick still isn't caught -- but every writer renames a fresh temp file into place, so a
# rewrite replaces a dirent and normally bumps the dir mtime; the residual needs a same-tick
# collision, deliberately left rather than paying git-style racy-clean logic on this hot path.)
# LRU: hits re-order, overflow evicts the oldest.
_DIR_STAT_MEMO: "OrderedDict[str, tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]]" = OrderedDict()


def _ops_dir_stat(repo: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """`(dirent_count, max_mtime_ns)` over `.sgt/ops/`, stat-only -- no file content reads."""
    ops_dir = Store(repo).ops_dir
    try:
        dir_mtime = ops_dir.stat().st_mtime_ns
    except OSError:
        return 0, -1
    key = os.path.realpath(ops_dir)
    # One scan feeds both the cheap count (the same-tick guard) and the per-entry stat (the
    # expensive part the memo actually skips on a hit).
    entries = [e for e in os.scandir(ops_dir) if e.is_file()]
    count = len(entries)
    memo = _DIR_STAT_MEMO.get(key)
    if memo is not None and memo[0] == (dir_mtime, count):
        _DIR_STAT_MEMO.move_to_end(key)
        return memo[1]
    max_mtime = -1
    for entry in entries:
        mtime = entry.stat().st_mtime_ns
        if mtime > max_mtime:
            max_mtime = mtime
    _DIR_STAT_MEMO[key] = ((dir_mtime, count), (count, max_mtime))
    if len(_DIR_STAT_MEMO) > 8:
        _DIR_STAT_MEMO.popitem(last=False)
    return count, max_mtime


def _stale_against_dir(repo: Path, miner_version, op_count, built_mtime_ns: int) -> bool:
    """Whether a snapshot with this `(miner_version, op_count, built_mtime_ns)` is stale against
    `.sgt/ops/`, checked stat-only (no op file reads). The single staleness rule, shared by
    `_is_stale_body` (which reads the fields off a loaded snapshot body) and `index_ops`' memo
    fast path (which reads them off the memoized parse), so the two cannot silently diverge if the
    rule ever gains a signal: a miner-version mismatch (catches `migrate ops-v3`), a dirent-count
    mismatch (catches sync ingest / prune), or a build timestamp at or before the newest op file's
    mtime (catches `Store.add`'s provenance-merge and `Store.attribute` rewrites, which bump mtime
    without changing count)."""
    if miner_version != MINER_VERSION:
        return True
    count, max_mtime = _ops_dir_stat(repo)
    if op_count != count:
        return True
    return built_mtime_ns <= max_mtime


def _is_stale_body(repo: Path, body: dict | None) -> bool:
    """`is_stale`'s check against an already-loaded (or absent) snapshot body -- factored out so
    `index_ops` can check staleness against the body it already read instead of reloading the
    file a second time."""
    if body is None:
        return True
    return _stale_against_dir(
        repo, body.get("miner_version"), body.get("op_count"), body.get("built_mtime_ns", -1)
    )

# `Store.all_ops` process memo: ops-dir realpath -> ((ops-dir mtime_ns, dirent_count), parsed ops).
# LRU (matches the codebase's OrderedDict cache convention); the dirent count keyed alongside the
# dir mtime is the same-tick backstop `sgt.core.opindex._ops_dir_stat` documents.
_ALL_OPS_MEMO: "OrderedDict[str, tuple[tuple[int, int], list[Op]]]" = OrderedDict()

# The directory's own mtime is the staleness signal: every writer lands entries via
        # rename into this directory (`_write_atomic`, git), and rename/add/delete bumps a
        # directory's mtime -- so an unchanged value proves the listing (and every entry) is what
        # it was when the memo was built. The dirent count is keyed alongside it as a same-tick
        # backstop (a write landing in the memoized read's mtime tick leaves the dir mtime
        # unchanged); the scan that produces `names` gives the count for free, and the memo still
        # spares the expensive part -- reading and decoding every op file (images hex included).
        sig = self.ops_dir.stat().st_mtime_ns
        names = sorted(e.name for e in os.scandir(self.ops_dir) if e.is_file())
        memo_key = os.path.realpath(self.ops_dir)
        memo = _ALL_OPS_MEMO.get(memo_key)
        if memo is not None and memo[0] == (sig, len(names)):
            _ALL_OPS_MEMO.move_to_end(memo_key)
            return list(memo[1])
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
            raws = list(pool.map(lambda n: (self.ops_dir / n).read_bytes(), names))
        ops: list[Op] = []
        for raw in raws:
            try:
                ops.append(_deserialize(raw))
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
                continue  # corrupt: skipped here, surfaced by fsck
        _ALL_OPS_MEMO[memo_key] = ((sig, len(names)), ops)
        if len(_ALL_OPS_MEMO) > 4:
            _ALL_OPS_MEMO.popitem(last=False)
        return list(ops)

def test_upset_in_many_equals_per_op_union_and_stays_valid_on_an_or_supported_set():
    """Pins the set-revert switch `revert(X) = ideal \\ upset_in_many(X)` (was `ideal \\ ∪
    upset_in(x)`) against the OR-support case reviewers flagged as a possible semantic change.

    A required version's producers form an OR-group (grounding needs *any one* of them), so a naive
    per-op union could under-remove an op kept alive only by a co-removed alternative -- leaving an
    ungrounded op that `_validated` would refuse. `consumer` here is OR-supported by the `(sym, v0)`
    producer group `{add, rev}`. In a *fork-free* ideal that group is chain-ordered, so grounding any
    producer implies grounding the chain-minimal one and the two forms coincide -- but the set form
    is the robust one: it's `ideal \\ _grounded(ideal - X)`, a superset of the union in general
    (removing more only ungrounds more) whose complement is a valid ideal by construction. So the
    switch can only ever turn a would-be refusal into a valid maximal edit, never silently
    over-remove. This pins both halves: equality with the union on every subset, and validity of the
    complement."""
    sym = "a.py::foo"
    add, mod, rev = _revert_chain(sym)
    consumer = make_op(
        {"b.py::c": (None, "v0")}, {"b.py::c": b"c"},
        requires=frozenset({(sym, "v0")}), provenance=("c3",),
    )
    ops = [add, mod, rev, consumer]
    ideal = {op.id for op in ops}
    assert is_valid_ideal(ops, ideal)

    for removed in ({mod.id}, {rev.id}, {mod.id, rev.id}, {add.id}, {add.id, rev.id}):
        union = frozenset().union(*(upset_in(x, ideal, ops) for x in removed))
        many = upset_in_many(removed, ideal, ops)
        assert many == union, removed  # no divergence on the OR-shaped case within a valid ideal
        assert is_valid_ideal(ops, ideal - many)  # and the complement is always a valid ideal

def test_commits_touching_follows_a_side_branch_deletion_across_a_merge(tmp_path):
    """`commits_touching` is scoped to a single path deliberately: a union pathspec over several
    paths is NOT a sound superset of each path's own walk, because git's history simplification
    follows only one TREESAME parent at a merge and a wider pathspec can flip which parent that is
    -- rerouting the walk away from the side branch that closed a symbol (the miner's rebirth
    lookback, U9, would then mis-mint a fresh birth instead of chaining). This pins the property
    the per-path walk guarantees: the side-branch commit that emptied `a.py` is reachable from the

    main = gb._git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD").stdout.strip()

    gb._git("checkout", "-q", "-b", "side")
    (tmp_path / "a.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")  # close foo on the side branch
    closing = gb.commit_all("chore: empty a.py")

    gb._git("checkout", "-q", main)
    (tmp_path / "b.py").write_text("def bar():\n    return 2\n", encoding="utf-8")

    assert closing in shas  # the side-branch deletion is on a.py's own-path history

    """The persistent `cat-file --batch` process is a long-lived optimization; if it dies (objects

    assert batch.read_many([(sha, "f.txt")]) == [b"content"]  # transparently restarted

# SGT Workbench — fixes + toolbar redesign

## Context

Reviewing the SGT Workbench webview (operating on `test-workspace/livehub`) surfaced four things. Investigation (3 explore agents, cited) changed the picture materially:

- **Two "bugs" don't exist in current `main`.** The bare-file footprint matcher (`sgt/loop/match.py` already joins bare-file steps via a `file:` key) and the plan-session lifecycle (`sgt/loop/plan.py` has `completed`, auto-close, `mark_done`, abandon, 7-day reaper; `plan_view` shows only `active_sessions`) are already fixed. The crowded "38/49 / 7 open plans" screenshot is **stale `.sgt/local` data from Jul 24**, not a live defect. → fix = pull latest + refresh the workspace data.
- **Three things are genuinely actionable, all frontend:**
  1. Row-label **overlap** in subsystem headers (`Platf…4`, `10feat · 1` overprint).
  2. **Empty vertical space** below the timeline rows.
  3. **Toolbar** clutter / lack of hierarchy (user wants it redesigned with taste).
  4. **Empty `CODE(I)` panel** ("No files under this path at this frontier") — turns out fixable frontend-only.

The deeper mis-clustering root cause (co-commit clustering fuses `livehub/conflict.py` into a test-labeled leaf, `sgt/lens/cluster.py:128-155`) is **out of scope** — it's a risky change to the clustering engine and only mislabels, not breaks. I'll fix the visible symptom and flag the rest.

## Approved decisions
- Plan chips → **one consolidated `Plans 38/49` chip** with a click popover listing sessions.
- Restyle depth → **bolder redesign**: segmented view control, oracle as a colored status dot, filled primary Save, stronger three-zone hierarchy (nav / status / actions).

---

## Step 0 — Pull latest + refresh data (no code)
1. `git pull --ff-only` on `semi-git` (confirm clean tree first; fall back to reporting if non-ff).
2. Refresh livehub projection so the workbench reflects current backend: re-run the sgt indexer/loop in `test-workspace/livehub` (regenerates `plan_sessions.json`, `tree.json`). Exact command confirmed at execution (likely `sgt map`/`sgt save` refresh path).

## Step 1 — Row-label overlap  (`media/workbench.js` `renderSwimlaneHeader` ~1035-1055)
Root cause (confirmed): SVG `<text>` with absolute `x`; the start-anchored `.swimlane-label` is truncated by a char budget `(labelW-30-ind)/6.5` that **ignores the meta width**, while the end-anchored `.swimlane-meta` (`text-anchor:end` at `x=plotX0-8≈labelW`) grows leftward into the same column.
- Build the meta string first, estimate its width (`meta.length * ~5.5px` at font-size 10), and **subtract it (plus an 8px gap) from the label's truncation budget**. One localized change; feature lanes (`renderLane`) are unaffected (no gutter meta).

## Step 2 — Empty vertical space  (`media/workbench.js` `ganttGeom` ~826-849, `renderTimeAxis` ~1149, render ~948)
Root cause (confirmed): the SVG height is fixed to content (`padT + rowCount·rowH + axis`); its scroll container `#rail` is stretched to full pane height by the `#app` flex column, so surplus shows as dead background.
- In `ganttGeom`: `naturalH = axisY + axisH`; `h = max(naturalH, rail.clientHeight - 16)`; **pin the axis to the bottom** (`axisY = h - axisH`). Rows stay top-anchored.
- In `renderTimeAxis`: draw the commit tick **gridlines full plot height** (`padT → axisY`) and let the frontier scrubber line span the full height. The former void becomes an honest, structured empty timeline with a usable full-height "now" scrubber — no half-filled look.

## Step 3 — Toolbar redesign  (`media/workbench.js` `renderTitlebar`/`renderPlanChip` ~672-755; `media/workbench.css` ~52-191, 715-759; `src/workbench.ts` static HTML ~75-92)
Three zones in `#titlebar` (flex, `align-items:center`), separated by thin `1px var(--line)` dividers; actions keep `margin-left:auto`:
- **Nav:** segmented `Timeline│Rail` control (single bordered group, active segment filled) + `HEAD ▾` composition button.
- **Status:** oracle as a small colored **status dot** + label (dot = `--accent` pending / `--land` pass / `--fail` fail / dim unconfigured), then a single **`Plans 38/49`** chip (mini ring, tabular-nums) replacing the N per-session chips, then a compact `◇N` drift/unplanned indicator.
- **Actions:** filled primary **Save** (`--vscode-button-background`), text Commit / Undo, inspector toggle.
- **Plans popover:** clicking the consolidated chip opens a small dropdown built from the existing `planMarks.sessions` data — one row per session (`○/●` glyph + name + `matched/total`, green `✓` when complete). New element + CSS; dismiss on outside-click.
- Uniform control height, 4px radii (reserve pill only for the status dot/chip), hover-only emphasis, all via existing `:root` tokens (no new color hues — respects the color=identity contract).

## Step 4 — Empty CODE(I) panel  (frontend-only)
Root cause (confirmed): host filters `fold.files` by the single majority-prefix `node.dir` (`tests/test_conflict.py`), excluding the feature's own op file `livehub/conflict.py`. But `_emit` **already sends `node.members`** (`sgt/api.py:991`), which include `livehub/conflict.py`.
- Filter by the feature's **member file-set ∪ dir prefix** instead of dir alone:
  `memberFiles = new Set((node.members||[]).map(m => m.split("::")[0]))` → keep a fold path if `memberFiles.has(path) || path.startsWith(node.dir)`.
- Apply at all **3 filter sites**: `src/workbench.ts:534` (`requestFold`), `media/workbench.js:2078` (playhead), `media/workbench.js:2104` (composition preview).
- `src/types.ts` (`MapNode` ~4-18): ensure `members: string[]` is typed.
- No Python / clustering changes. Flag separately: the leaf is still *labeled* "Conflict Test Suite" while owning production code (mis-clustering) — recommend a later, dedicated fix.

## Step 5 — Build + verify
- Compile the extension (host TS): `npm run compile` (or the esbuild script) in `editor/vscode` — `media/*.js|css` are static assets, but `workbench.ts`/`types.ts` need compiling, and the bundle has gone stale before.
- No backend edits → Python suite untouched; run a focused `pytest` on `sgt/lens` only if Step 0's refresh reveals a data issue (per memory: never add xdist / weaken tests).
- Manual verify in VS Code: reload window → open **SGT Workbench**.
  - Overlap: subsystem headers show label + meta with no overprint at narrow/wide pane widths.
  - Empty space: no dead zone; gridlines + bottom axis fill height.
  - Toolbar: three zones, single Plans chip, popover lists sessions, filled Save.
  - CODE(I): select the "Conflict Test Suite" feature → panel now shows `livehub/conflict.py` (not "No files under this path").

- `editor/vscode/src/workbench.ts` — steps 3, 4
- `editor/vscode/src/types.ts` — step 4
- (no Python source edits; `sgt` only re-run to refresh livehub data)

def test_map_view_renders_a_shared_feature_under_its_one_canonical_parent(tmp_path):
    """The tree is a DAG: an authored feature can be spliced under more than one subsystem, so its
    id is listed in several parents' `children` while carrying a single canonical `parent`. `map_view`
    must render it once -- under that one parent -- so the feature tree, the workbench timeline, and
    the TUI agree, and it must not double-count the shared ops in every ancestor's `op_count` rollup.

    Corpus fixtures are all single-node, so this reshapes a built `tree.json` into a minimal DAG
    (LEAF listed under both N1 and N2, canonical parent N1) and checks the projection collapses it."""
    from sgt.lens import tree
    from sgt.lens.map import build_map

    repo = _mined(tmp_path, "mixed_coverage")
    build_map(repo)
    res = tree.load(repo)
    real_op = next(iter(res["op_leaf"]))  # a real op so leaf_op_count picks it up

    def node(nid, parent, children, label, members=()):
        return {"id": nid, "parent": parent, "children": list(children), "depth": 0,
                "members": list(members), "size": max(1, len(members)), "dir": "",
                "label": label, "why": "", "split_reason": None}

    leaf = "f-shared"
    res["nodes"] = {
        "N0": node("N0", None, ["N1", "N2"], "root"),
        "N1": node("N1", "N0", [leaf], "SubA"),
        "N2": node("N2", "N0", [leaf], "SubB"),  # DAG: also lists the leaf, but is not its parent
        leaf: node(leaf, "N1", [], "Shared", members=["x"]),
    }
    res["roots"] = ["N0"]
    res["op_leaf"] = {real_op: leaf}
    tree.save(repo, res)

    v = map_view(repo)
    by_id = {n["id"]: n for n in v["nodes"]}
    # the shared leaf is rendered under its canonical parent only, never the borrowing subsystem
    assert by_id["N1"]["children"] == [leaf]
    assert by_id["N2"]["children"] == []
    assert [n["id"] for n in v["nodes"] if leaf in n["children"]] == ["N1"]
    # and its single op is counted once at the root, not once per listing parent
    assert by_id[leaf]["op_count"] == 1
    assert by_id["N2"]["op_count"] == 0
    assert by_id["N0"]["op_count"] == 1

# Code Review — `map_view` shared-feature de-duplication

**Scope:** working-tree changes (`git diff HEAD`) — `sgt/api.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `editor/vscode/media/workbench.css`
**Reviewers (7):** correctness, testing, maintainability, project-standards, agent-native, learnings, api-contract
**Verdict:** APPROVE — the change is correct and well-placed. One consistency gap the change itself introduced was fixed and tested during review; two report-only items remain.

## What the change does

The feature tree is a DAG: an authored feature can be spliced under more than one subsystem, so a
shared leaf appears in several parents' `children` while carrying one canonical `parent`. The diff
adds `canonical_children(nid)` in `sgt.api.map_view` and routes `children`, `op_count`, and the
session rollup through it, so a shared feature renders once, under its one parent, and its ops
aren't double-counted in every ancestor. `map_view` is the single projection every surface reads
(VS Code webview, TUI, CLI `--json`), so the fix lands atomically with no per-surface logic to keep
in sync. It also repairs a latent gap from `dda1d71`: that commit deduped duplicate *rows*
client-side (`seen` sets in `graph.py`/`workbench.js`) but left the *op-count numbers* inflated for
raw `map_view`/CLI consumers — this fixes the numbers at the source.

### Finding 1 — the `kind`/canonical-children inconsistency (top finding)

Certain at the code level (verifiable from the diff alone) and independently flagged by four
reviewers. Five consumer touch-points, all verified by direct inspection, mishandle a
`kind:"subsystem"` + `children:[]` row:

- `featuresTree.ts:26` — collapsibility from `children.length` -> renders as a leaf
- `featuresTree.ts:38` + `package.json:125-128` — actions gated on `viewItem == sgtFeature` -> the row loses previewRevert/revert/restore/edit
- `sgt/tui/app.py:651` — expand gated on `kind == "feature"` -> can't drill into member symbols
- `sgt/tui/graph.py:88-99` and `workbench.js:88-92` — recursion gated on `kind == "subsystem"` -> node iterates its empty children and vanishes from the timeline

**Caveat (reachability):** whether the tree builder actually produces a borrower-only node (zero
canonical children) in live data is unconfirmed — the test constructs the shape synthetically (node
`N2`). So this is a latent inconsistency the diff introduced, certain in the code but of unknown
live frequency. The fix is safe either way: for every node that is *not* borrower-only,
`canonical_children == raw children`, so the projection is byte-identical; only borrower-only nodes
change.

**Applied:** `sgt/api.py:997` now reads `"kind": "feature" if not canonical_children(nid) else
"subsystem"`, mirroring the sibling lines and matching the diff's own new comment (946-952). Added
`assert by_id["N2"]["kind"] == "feature"` / `["N1"]["kind"] == "subsystem"` to the DAG test —
confirmed the assertion fails on the pre-fix line and passes after. Full `test_api.py` (50) and the
graph/segment/decision layout suites pass.

**Reported, not applied — `feature_count` (sgt/api.py:1023):** reviewers disagree. Correctness
says leave it (it counts structural leaves; a borrower-only shell isn't a real feature). Maintain-
ability/testing say canonicalize for consistency. It's an aggregate summary with no per-node
consumer divergence, so it's a design call, not a safe mechanical autofix. Note: after the `kind`
fix, `kind` and `feature_count` now use different child notions for borrower-only nodes — pick one.

### Finding 2 — `node_sessions` rollup untested

A meaningful assertion needs the shared leaf to carry real attributed session data, which comes
from `opindex` attribution keyed by op-id and can't be injected via `tree.save` — so it's fixture

### Finding 3 — CSS opacity tweaks (scope note)

The three `workbench.css` opacity bumps are mechanically visible in the diff and look like an

## Residual risks

- **Canonical-parent stability across rebuilds.** The whole scheme assumes a shared leaf's single
  `parent` pointer is stable across `build_map`/`_splice`. If a rebuild reassigns it, a shared
  feature silently jumps subsystems. Out of this diff's scope; worth a targeted test.
- **`grid_view` vs the DAG shape** is unverified — the learnings hypothesis of a sibling raw-children
  walk (`_grid_labels`) did not confirm a matching site in `api.py`. Low priority.

## What's solid

- Root-cause fix in the one shared projection layer, not per-surface workarounds (agent-native PASS).
- `workbench.js` `rollup()` walks `childrenOf` (now canonical) and benefits with zero JS change.
- `_authored_leaf_claims`/`feature_edges` resolve via member-set index, so they were never exposed
  to the double-listing bug and correctly needed no change.

def _shared_feature_dag(tmp_path):
    """Build a minimal DAG for the shared-feature projection tests. Corpus fixtures are all
    single-node, so we reshape a freshly built `tree.json` by hand: a LEAF listed under *both* N1
    and N2 (a DAG) but canonically parented to N1 -- N2 only borrows it. Returns
    (repo, leaf_id, real_op_id); the caller reads `map_view(repo)`."""
    from sgt.lens import tree
    from sgt.lens.map import build_map

    repo = _mined(tmp_path, "mixed_coverage")
    build_map(repo)
    res = tree.load(repo)
    real_op = next(iter(res["op_leaf"]))  # a real op so leaf_op_count / attribution pick it up

    def node(nid, parent, children, label, members=()):
        return {"id": nid, "parent": parent, "children": list(children), "depth": 0,
                "members": list(members), "size": max(1, len(members)), "dir": "",
                "label": label, "why": "", "split_reason": None}

    leaf = "f-shared"
    res["nodes"] = {
        "N0": node("N0", None, ["N1", "N2"], "root"),
        "N1": node("N1", "N0", [leaf], "SubA"),
        "N2": node("N2", "N0", [leaf], "SubB"),  # DAG: also lists the leaf, but is not its parent
        leaf: node(leaf, "N1", [], "Shared", members=["x"]),
    }
    res["roots"] = ["N0"]
    res["op_leaf"] = {real_op: leaf}
    tree.save(repo, res)
    return repo, leaf, real_op


def test_map_view_renders_a_shared_feature_under_its_one_canonical_parent(tmp_path):
    """The tree is a DAG: an authored feature can be spliced under more than one subsystem, so its
    id is listed in several parents' `children` while carrying a single canonical `parent`. `map_view`
    must render it once -- under that one parent -- so the feature tree, the workbench timeline, and
    the TUI agree, and it must not double-count the shared ops in every ancestor's `op_count` rollup."""
    repo, leaf, _ = _shared_feature_dag(tmp_path)

    v = map_view(repo)
    by_id = {n["id"]: n for n in v["nodes"]}
    # the shared leaf is rendered under its canonical parent only, never the borrowing subsystem
    assert by_id["N1"]["children"] == [leaf]
    assert by_id["N2"]["children"] == []
    assert [n["id"] for n in v["nodes"] if leaf in n["children"]] == ["N1"]
    # and its single op is counted once at the root, not once per listing parent
    assert by_id[leaf]["op_count"] == 1
    assert by_id["N2"]["op_count"] == 0
    assert by_id["N0"]["op_count"] == 1
    # `kind` must agree with the now-canonical `children`: a borrower-only node (all its listed
    # children are borrowed, none canonically its own) is a leaf, not a subsystem. Consumers gate on
    # this pair -- VS Code tree actions/collapsibility, TUI expand, timeline recursion -- so a
    # `kind:"subsystem"` row emitting `children:[]` is mishandled (drops actions / vanishes).
    assert by_id["N2"]["kind"] == "feature"
    assert by_id["N1"]["kind"] == "subsystem"
    # `feature_count` counts feature nodes, so it must agree with the canonical `kind`: the borrower-
    # only N2 and the shared leaf are the two features here (raw children would miscount N2 as a
    # subsystem and report 1).
    assert v["feature_count"] == 2
    # Canonical de-duplication must yield a proper forest, which is what makes each node's canonical
    # parent well-defined (the residual-risk the whole scheme rests on): every non-root node appears
    # in exactly one node's emitted `children`, and that node is its `parent`. Reverting `children`
    # to raw would list the shared leaf under both N1 and N2 (listers == ["N1", "N2"]) -- so this
    # bites the double-listing directly, and also flags an orphan (a parent that fails to list its
    # child would give listers == []).
    for nid, nd in by_id.items():
        if nd["parent"] is None:
            continue
        listers = [p for p in by_id if nid in by_id[p]["children"]]
        assert listers == [nd["parent"]], (nid, listers)


def test_map_view_rolls_sessions_up_through_the_canonical_parent_only(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """`node_sessions` must roll provenance up through *canonical* children, exactly like `op_count`:
    a session attributed to the shared leaf reaches its one canonical ancestor chain (N1 -> N0), not
    the borrowing subsystem N2. Sessions come from `opindex` attribution keyed by op-id and can't be
    injected via `tree.save`, so we attach one to the shared leaf's op. Reverting `node_sessions` to
    raw children would leak the session onto N2 -- this asserts it does not."""
    import dataclasses

    from sgt.core import opindex
    from sgt.core.op import Attribution

    repo, leaf, real_op = _shared_feature_dag(tmp_path)

    real_ops = opindex.index_ops(repo)
    assert any(op.id == real_op for op in real_ops)  # the leaf's op is attributable

    def with_session(_repo):
        return [
            dataclasses.replace(op, attribution=op.attribution + (Attribution(sha=op.id, session="sess-1"),))
            if op.id == real_op else op
            for op in real_ops
        ]

    monkeypatch.setattr(opindex, "index_ops", with_session)

    v = map_view(repo)
    by_id = {n["id"]: n for n in v["nodes"]}
    assert by_id[leaf]["sessions"] == ["sess-1"]  # attributed directly to the shared leaf
    assert by_id["N1"]["sessions"] == ["sess-1"]  # its one canonical parent rolls it up
    assert by_id["N0"]["sessions"] == ["sess-1"]  # ...to the root

# In-situ save preview + transition (SGT Workbench)

## Context

The user (UX-minded) is confused because the workbench never shows the *consequence* of an
action. When you `sgt save`, ops are committed silently and the graph only reflects it on the next
full refresh — there is no visible causal link between "I saved" and "the graph changed." The user
wants a **pending commit** rendered in-situ: before saving, the affected features should show a
"ghost checkpoint" of the work that *would* land; on save, that ghost should visibly resolve into a
real checkpoint.

This is build #1 of the agreed workflow-legibility redesign (see memory
`workflow-legibility-redesign`). Decision locked: **semantic-primary, op drill-down** — this slice
stays at feature granularity (which features gain work), not op/symbol reconciliation.

Success criterion: with uncommitted work in the tree, each affected feature lane shows a **dashed
ghost car at the "now" frontier**; running Save turns those dashed cars **solid with a short
transition**, and the ghost disappears. No new op-level jargon is surfaced.

## Approach

Three layers: a new read-only projection (Python), a host call that folds it into the state
message (TypeScript), and a dashed ghost-car render + solidify transition (webview JS/CSS).

### 1. Server: `save_preview_view(repo)` — new projection in `sgt/api.py`

A pure-ish read that answers "which features would gain ops if I saved now," modeled on
`_project_verb_preview` / `_affected_rows` (api.py:391-410, 615-661).

Recipe (all functions confirmed to exist and be non-mutating except the `.sgt/`-cache note below):
1. `mined = get(repo)`, `recorded = current_ideal(repo)` (`sgt/core/lens.py:593,320`); delta =
   `mined.op_ids - recorded.op_ids` — the same equality `porcelain.py:142` uses for "nothing_new".
2. `ops = opindex.index_ops(repo)` (footprint-only; same source `map_view` uses, api.py:964);
   `uncommitted_ops = [by_id[i] for i in delta]`.
3. `nodes = sgt.lens.tree.load(repo)["nodes"]`.
4. `op_leaf = tree.assign_ops_to_leaves(nodes, uncommitted_ops)` (`sgt/lens/tree.py:392`) — **pure**,
   returns `{op_id: leaf_id}`, omits ops touching no owned symbol. Invert → `{feature_id: [op_ids]}`.
5. Ops absent from step 4 = the **new-work bucket** (touch no existing feature). Report them
   separately with a count; do not attempt lane-minting prediction in v1 (defer `assign_new_symbols`).

Return shape (mirrors verb-preview rollups):
```
{ "affected": [ {"feature_id", "op_count", "op_ids"} ... ],  # existing features gaining ops
  "new_work_count": int,                                     # ops with no current feature
  "total_op_count": int }                                    # = len(delta)
```
When delta is empty, `affected: []` — the "nothing pending" state renders no ghosts.

**Caveat to honor (flag in code comment):** `get()` is not fully side-effect-free — `_sync`
persists mined ops into `.sgt/` store/opindex + sync cache and advances the witness
(lens.py:500-589). It does **not** create a git commit and does **not** touch the recorded ideal.
This matches what `sgt save`/`status` already do on the working tree, so it's acceptable for a
preview, but the docstring must say so (no silent "read-only" claim).

Expose via the existing CLI/MCP JSON surface the extension already reads (same pattern as other
`*_view` projections — add the `--json` entrypoint next to where `state_view`/`drift_view` are wired
in `sgt/cli`).

### 2. Host: fold preview into the state message — `editor/vscode/src/workbench.ts`

`pushState()` (ts:116) already reads `composeView`/`gridView` and posts `{type:"state", compose}`.
Add one call to the new projection there and attach it: `postMessage({type:"state", compose, savePreview})`.
Folding it into the existing state message (rather than a new `savePreview`/seq round-trip) means
the ghost is just part of every render — the most "in-situ" behavior and no correlation plumbing.

- Add `savePreview()` to `src/store.ts` next to `composeView()`/`driftView()` (same subprocess-JSON
  idiom).
- If the extra mine per refresh is a perf concern, debounce or compute lazily — but default to
  computing it in `pushState` so the ghost is always live. (Note for implementer: verify refresh
  cadence; `store.onDidChange` already drives full re-renders on file save.)

### 3. Webview: dashed ghost cars + solidify transition — `editor/vscode/media/workbench.js` + `workbench.css`

**Data:** store the incoming `savePreview` in a module var alongside `planMarks` (built in the
`state` message handler, js:2398-2420), keyed `byFeature[feature_id] = {op_count}`.

**Render ghost cars:** in `renderLane` (js:1068), after `renderCars` (js:872-945), add a pass that —
for each lane with `savePreview.byFeature[l.id]` — draws one dashed car:
- Positioned at the **"now" frontier** (right of the last committed car): `x = geom.xOf(maxCommit)`
  extending to the plot right edge, since uncommitted ops have no commit index yet.
- `<g class="gcar-wrap gcar-pending">` + `rect.gcar.gcar-pending`, `fill: laneColor(l.id)`, with a
  `<title>` like `"+N pending — will land on save"` and the `+N` count.
- Mirror the existing pending-plan idiom (`renderLaneBadges` dashed `.gbar-plan` underline +
  `.gbar-plan-count`, js:1138-1144) for visual family.
- A subsystem/meta-lane aggregates its children's pending counts (same rollup shape as its cars).

**Solidify transition (ghost → solid on save):** `renderGraph` does `rail.innerHTML=""` and fully
rebuilds, so continuity is via a class toggle across renders (the approach the `.plan-ring-fill`
transition uses, css:805). Copy the `prevKnownPlanSteps` bookkeeping pattern (js:767-782):
- Track `prevPendingFeatures` (set of feature ids that had a ghost last render).
- After a save, those ops are now committed → they render as normal solid cars. For any lane that
  was pending last render and now has a *new* real car, add an entering class `gcar-landing` to
  that car; CSS transitions it from the dashed/low-opacity ghost look to solid over ~300ms, then
  the class is dropped on the next render.
- Gate with the existing `prefersReducedMotion()` helper (js:813) and the reduced-motion CSS block.

**CSS (`workbench.css`):**
- `.gcar-pending` — dashed stroke + reduced `fill-opacity` (mirror `.gcar-thematic` css:436 +
  `.gbar-plan` css:535).
- `.gcar.gcar-landing` — transition on `fill-opacity`/`stroke-dasharray` for the solidify.
- Add both classes to the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block (css:951).
- Do **not** touch `.ghost-blast`/`.ghost-target`/`.ghost-foundation` — owned by verb-arming and
  wiped by `clearGhosts` on every mouseleave.

### Out of scope for this slice (later builds in the redesign)
- Semantic plan rewrite, stalled-step "Resume with Claude Code", drift-codelens removal, plain
  `sgt save` CLI output — all tracked separately in the redesign backlog.
- New-work lane-mint prediction (`assign_new_symbols`) — v1 just counts new-work ops.
- Plan-step "this save completes step X" overlay — the existing `planMarks` dashed decoration
  already hints it; a richer tie-in comes with the semantic-plan build.

## Files
- `sgt/api.py` — add `save_preview_view(repo)` (model on `_project_verb_preview`/`_affected_rows`).
- `sgt/cli/…` — wire the `--json` entrypoint (same place other `*_view`s are exposed).
- `editor/vscode/src/store.ts` — add `savePreview()`.
- `editor/vscode/src/workbench.ts` — call it in `pushState`, attach to the `state` message.
- `editor/vscode/media/workbench.js` — store preview data; ghost-car render pass in `renderLane`;
  `gcar-landing` entering-class bookkeeping.
- `editor/vscode/media/workbench.css` — `.gcar-pending`, `.gcar-landing`, reduced-motion entries.
- Tests: `tests/test_api.py` — a `save_preview_view` case (dirty tree → correct `affected`/`new_work`
  split; clean tree → empty).

## Verification
1. **Backend, isolated:** in a scratch sgt repo, edit a file touching an existing feature's symbol +
   add a brand-new symbol; run the new projection via CLI `--json`. Assert the existing feature
   appears in `affected` with the right `op_count` and the new symbol lands in `new_work_count`.
   Clean tree → `affected: []`. Add to `tests/test_api.py` (run focused per memory
   `test-suite-slow-subprocess`: `pytest tests/test_api.py -k save_preview`).
2. **End-to-end in VS Code:** open the workbench on a repo with uncommitted work → confirm dashed
   ghost cars appear on the affected lanes at the frontier with `+N`. Click Save → confirm the
   ghost cars solidify with the transition and the `+N` clears. Toggle reduced-motion → confirm the
   transition is disabled but the final solid state is correct.
3. **No regression:** hover a car to arm revert preview → confirm `.ghost-blast` etc. still paint
   and clear independently of the save ghosts (the two ghost systems don't interfere).

def test_save_preview_view_splits_affected_features_from_new_work(tmp_path):
    """The in-situ save preview answers "which features gain ops if I save now". A clean tree has
    nothing pending; uncommitted work that reworks an existing feature's symbol lands in `affected`
    (attributed to that feature's leaf), while a brand-new symbol -- a member of no built leaf --
    falls into the `new_work` bucket. `total_op_count` accounts for both."""
    from sgt.lens.map import build_map
    from sgt.lens.tree import load as load_tree

    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    gb, _ = init_store(repo)
    (repo / "a.py").write_text("def foo():\n    return 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    gb.commit_all("add foo")
    get(repo)
    build_map(repo)

    # the leaf that owns the committed symbol -- affected work should attribute here
    nodes = load_tree(repo)["nodes"]
    foo_leaf = next(nid for nid, nd in nodes.items()
                    if not nd["children"] and "a.py::foo" in nd["members"])

    # clean tree: nothing would land on save
    assert save_preview_view(repo) == {"affected": [], "new_work_count": 0, "total_op_count": 0}

    # uncommitted: rework the existing symbol (-> its feature) + add a brand-new one (-> new work)
    (repo / "a.py").write_text(
        "def foo():\n    return 2\n\n\ndef bar():\n    return 3\n", encoding="utf-8")

    v = save_preview_view(repo)
    assert v["total_op_count"] > 0
    affected_ids = {row["feature_id"] for row in v["affected"]}
    assert foo_leaf in affected_ids  # the reworked symbol's feature is flagged
    assert v["new_work_count"] >= 1  # `bar` belongs to no built leaf
    # the split is exhaustive: every pending op is either attributed or new work
    attributed = sum(row["op_count"] for row in v["affected"])
    assert attributed + v["new_work_count"] == v["total_op_count"]

# Plan status + Resume (SGT Workbench)

## Context

This is build #2 of the workflow-legibility redesign (memory `workflow-legibility-redesign`;
build #1 — in-situ save preview — shipped 2026-07-27). The user, applying Apple HIG, wants three
things: you always know **what you're looking at**, **what you can do next**, and the **flow is
streamlined**.

Today a plan that an agent started and then abandoned mid-way is invisible as such. Sessions carry
only `active`/`completed` status and steps only `pending`/`matched` — there is **no interrupted
state**. A stalled plan looks identical to a healthy in-progress one, and after 7 days of silence
it is silently reaped (`sweep_stale_sessions`, STALE_SECONDS) with no chance for the user to act.
The user explicitly asked to see "semantic plan nodes that are not actually being worked on /
were interrupted, so I can ask Claude Code to resume."

**Outcome:** each active plan is classified (derived, no new stored state) as **building** or
**stalled**; stalled plans are surfaced distinctly and offer a single clear next action —
**"Resume in terminal"**, which relaunches the interrupted Claude Code session via
`claude --resume`. Success: with an interrupted plan (pending steps, gone quiet, no work in
flight), the workbench marks it *stalled* and one click opens a terminal that resumes that
Claude Code conversation.

**Locked context:** decision "semantic-primary, op drill-down" still holds — this stays at
feature/plan granularity. Resume mechanism confirmed with the user + verified against the Claude
Code CLI (`claude --resume <id>` resumes a specific session interactively; bare `--resume` opens a
picker; the agent's own session id is only reliably readable via `$CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`
when Remote Control is active — so the id link is best-effort with a picker fallback).

## Approach

Derived state (no migration, no new writer), a Resume command that shells `claude --resume` into a
terminal, and surfacing on the plan surfaces the user already reads.

### 1. Backend: derive `stalled`/`building` in `plan_view` — `sgt/api.py`

`plan_view` (api.py:1404) already computes `compute_checkpoint(repo)` and reads each session's
`last_activity_ts`. Classify each **active** session (compact mode) with no new persistence:

- `building` — has ≥1 pending step AND (a live checkpoint candidate names this session in
  `checkpoint.matches`, i.e. uncommitted work is flowing toward it) OR `now - last_activity_ts <=
  STALLED_SECONDS`.
- `stalled` — has ≥1 pending step AND no live candidate for this session AND
  `now - last_activity_ts > STALLED_SECONDS`.
- (`completed` sessions already drop out via `plan.active_sessions`; guard a fully-matched active
  session to not read as stalled.)

The candidate check (not age alone) is what prevents flagging an agent that is mid-edit or a
freshly-`intake`d plan. Add to each compact session dict:
`derived_status`, `pending_count`, and `remaining_titles` (pending step titles — small,
activity-bounded; the UI needs them without a `full` fetch). Also surface an existing
`claude_session_id` field if present (see §5).

Add `STALLED_SECONDS` next to `STALE_SECONDS` in `sgt/loop/plan.py` (one hardcoded constant, no
config knob — default `3600` = 1h: long enough not to flag an agent pausing between steps, short
enough to surface a truly-abandoned plan in the same working session). Import it in `api.py`.

Erring toward flagging is deliberate (HIG): a false "stalled" that offers Resume is harmless; a
missed stall silently reaped after 7 days is the real pain.

### 2. Resume command — `editor/vscode/src/commands.ts` + `workbench.ts`

Register `sgt.resumePlan(sessionId)`:
1. Read the session from `store.planView()` (its `claude_session_id`, `plan_text`, remaining titles).
2. Open/reuse a VS Code terminal ("sgt resume") and `sendText`:
   - `claude --resume <claude_session_id>` when a captured Claude session id exists (direct
     relaunch of the exact conversation — its plan context is already restored, so no prompt
     re-injection needed).
   - else `claude --resume` (bare) — Claude Code's own picker. sgt has already shown *which* plan
     stalled and its remaining steps, so the user selects the right session.
   - `terminal.show()` so it's focused. Do **not** auto-run a non-interactive prompt — resuming
     restores context; the user continues by typing.
3. `workbench.ts onMessage`: add `case "resumePlan"` → `executeCommand("sgt.resumePlan",
   msg.sessionId)` (mirrors the existing `openPlanDiff`/`confirmCheckpoint` cases, ts:207-211).

Candid tradeoff (in a code comment): `claude` must be on PATH; if it isn't, the terminal shows a
command-not-found — acceptable and exactly what the user asked for ("relaunch that session in their
terminal"). sgt never authors code itself, so handing back to the real Claude Code session is the
correct on-ramp.

### 3. Webview surfacing — `editor/vscode/media/workbench.js` + `workbench.css`

- **`collectPlanMarks`** (js:538): thread `derivedStatus` + `remainingTitles` into each
  `sessions[]` entry (it already builds `sessionId`/`planText`/`matchedCount`/`stepCount`).
- **Plans popover** (`renderPlansPopover`, js:747): stalled rows get a distinct paused glyph
  (`⏸`, muted) instead of `○`/`●`, and a small **"Resume"** button posting
  `{type:"resumePlan", sessionId}`. Building rows unchanged.
- **Session inspector card** (`renderPlanSessionCard`, js:1976): when `derivedStatus === "stalled"`,
  below the `N/M step(s) landed` meta add an "Interrupted — N step(s) not built" line and a
  prominent **"Resume in terminal"** button (the primary, discoverable next-action). This is the
  main HIG affordance: clear label of the state + one clear action.
- **CSS**: a muted `.plans-pop-row.stalled` treatment and a `.plan-resume` button style. Minimal;
  reuse existing `.action` button styling where possible.

### 4. Status bar + quick pick — `editor/vscode/src/plan.ts`

def test_plan_view_derives_building_and_stalled_from_activity_and_candidates(tmp_path):
    """A pending plan is `building` while recently active, `stalled` once it goes quiet past
    STALLED_SECONDS with no work flowing toward it, and `building` again -- age notwithstanding --
    the moment a checkpoint candidate names it. `claude_session_id` is surfaced for the Resume
    hand-off, and `pending_count`/`remaining_titles` come along without a `full` fetch."""
    import time

    from sgt.loop.plan import STALLED_SECONDS

    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    gb, _ = init_store(repo)
    (repo / "a.py").write_text("def foo():\n    return 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    gb.commit_all("add foo")
    get(repo)

    # Recent activity, pending step, no candidate -> building.
    _seed_plan_session(repo, gb, session_id="fresh", last_activity_ts=time.time(),
                       claude_session_id="sess-abc")
    session = plan_view(repo)["sessions"][0]
    assert session["derived_status"] == "building"
    assert session["pending_count"] == 1
    assert session["remaining_titles"] == ["touch foo"]
    assert session["claude_session_id"] == "sess-abc"

    # Same session backdated well past STALLED_SECONDS with still no candidate -> stalled.
    table = plan_mod._load_sessions(repo)
    table["fresh"]["last_activity_ts"] = time.time() - STALLED_SECONDS - 60
    plan_mod._save_sessions(repo, table)
    assert plan_view(repo)["sessions"][0]["derived_status"] == "stalled"

    # Commit work matching the predicted footprint -> a live candidate names the session, so it
    # reads `building` again despite the stale activity timestamp (candidate overrides age).
    (repo / "a.py").write_text("def foo():\n    return 2\n", encoding="utf-8")
    gb.commit_all("touch foo")
    get(repo)
    view = plan_view(repo)
    assert view["checkpoint"]["matches"], "expected a checkpoint candidate for the matching work"
    assert view["sessions"][0]["derived_status"] == "building"
